sources.entry: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python by Al Sweigart

summary.name: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python
summary.one_liner: A free-to-read, Creative Commons-licensed beginner Python book by Al Sweigart (third edition) that teaches Python through practical tasks like file handling, web scraping, spreadsheets, PDFs, email, and GUI automation.
keywords: automate the boring stuff with python
use_cases: Renaming and organizing files in bulk
Updating Excel or Google Sheets data automatically
Splitting, merging, or extracting text from PDFs and Word documents
Sending scheduled email or text notifications
Automating keyboard and mouse actions in applications
summary.what_it_does: The book teaches Python from the basics (strings, lists, dictionaries, control flow, functions) through regular expressions, then applies it to automation projects. Later chapters cover file and folder operations, command line programs, web scraping, Excel, Google Sheets, SQLite, PDF and Word documents, CSV/JSON/XML, scheduling, email and push notifications, images and graphs, OCR, and controlling the keyboard and mouse. A companion workbook offers chapter-by-chapter exercises and miniprojects. The book is free to read online under a Creative Commons license.
notable: Free to read online under a Creative Commons license, with a free ebook option
Written for readers with no prior programming experience
Companion Workbook with chapter-by-chapter exercises and miniprojects
Author maintains open source projects PyAutoGUI and pyperclip
caveats: Print and other ebook editions are sold through retailers; the workbook and video course are paid products
Video course discount is a promotional code; the video course covers much but not all of the 1st edition
Review copy offers require at least $50 in Amazon purchases and a commitment to write a review
